ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.parent_proof_nl:
Fix an integer n > 1, and define f_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k. Let r be any real number with 0 <= r < 1, and set m = floor(nr). We must show f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).

Since m = floor(nr), we have m <= nr < m+1. Dividing by n > 0 gives m/n <= r. Therefore, for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n, multiplying by k preserves the inequality:
k(m/n) <= kr.
Because the floor function is monotone nondecreasing on R, it follows that
floor(k(m/n)) <= floor(kr)
for every k = 1, ..., n.

Also, m is an integer, so
floor(n(m/n)) = floor(m) = m = floor(nr).

Now compare the two values:
f_n(r) = floor(nr) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kr)/k
<= m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(m/n))/k
= floor(n(m/n)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(m/n))/k
= f_n(m/n).

This is exactly the desired inequality.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and satisfies n > 1
r is real and satisfies 0 <= r < 1
m is defined as floor of n times r, hence m is an integer
m divided by n is an input value for f_n (assumes f_n is defined on it)
parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every real r with 0 <= r < 1, if m is defined as the floor of n times r, then f_n(r) is at most f_n(m divided by n).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with 0 <= r < 1
let m be floor of n times r
claim: f_n(r) <= f_n(m divided by n)
